questions.q: If you declare a method or variable with no access modifier at all, what visibility does it get?
options: global
public
private -- this is the default
protected
questions.explain: By default, a method or variable is visible only to the Apex code within the defining class -- if you don't specify an access modifier, the method or variable is private.

questions.q: How does Apex's public access modifier differ from Java's public?
options: They behave identically in both languages
Apex's public only makes a member visible within the same application namespace, not across all applications like Java's public -- that broader visibility requires global instead
Apex has no public modifier at all
public in Apex is more permissive than global
questions.explain: In Apex, the public access modifier isn't the same as it is in Java -- this was done to keep applications separate; to get Java-style public visibility, you must use global.

questions.q: Which access modifier can only be used on instance methods and member variables, not static ones?
options: private
protected
global
public
questions.explain: protected means the method or variable is visible to inner classes and extending classes, but you can only use this access modifier for instance methods and member variables.

questions.q: If class MyClass has a static variable myStaticVariable, and myClassInstance is an instance of MyClass, is myClassInstance.myStaticVariable a legal expression?
options: Yes, static variables can always be read through any instance
No -- a class static variable can't be accessed through an instance of that class; use MyClass.myStaticVariable instead
Only if the variable is also marked public
Only inside a trigger context
questions.explain: A class static variable can't be accessed through an instance of that class -- myClassInstance.myStaticVariable isn't a legal expression; you must refer to it as MyClass.myStaticVariable.

questions.q: What is true about the lifetime of a static variable's value in Apex?
options: It persists forever across the entire org for all users
It's static only within the scope of the Apex transaction and is reset across transaction boundaries
It resets every time any method in the class runs
It can only be set once per org, ever
questions.explain: A static variable is static only within the scope of the Apex transaction, not across the server or the entire organization -- its value persists within a single transaction and resets across transaction boundaries.
